nodes.label: clean_description() HTML cleaning
nodes.rationale: Strips page-builder scaffolding (Magento PageBuilder, Avada/Fusion Builder, wrapper divs, <style>), keeps headings/lists/paragraphs. Default is cleaned HTML; the sample keeps raw markup. Open question for the client: cleaned vs raw.

nodes.label: Option1/2 value resolution
nodes.rationale: Woo option values come from parent attributes[].terms joined to variations by id; fallback = variation label string; fallback = synthesised grid. Option1 Name = Colour for multi-colour products, Title for single-variant; single-variant Option1 Value = Default Title.

nodes.label: Matrixify multi-row product model
nodes.rationale: Row 1 carries product-level fields + variant 1 + image 1; one row per further variant; trailing rows carry only Handle + Image Src + Image Position for gallery overflow. Product-level fields appear only on the first row.

nodes.label: Shopify Submission Format column map
nodes.rationale: Source of truth is vertx_product_submission_sample.csv, a Matrixify (Excelify) sheet, not a native Shopify CSV. Column order does not matter to Matrixify, names do; unused columns can be omitted. The header row is reproduced verbatim from the sample.

nodes.label: Oakley SI sunglasses category page fixture
nodes.norm_label: oakley si sunglasses category page fixture
nodes.rationale: Captured SAP Commerce Cloud PLP HTML (pageType Plp) for /en-us/category/sunglasses, build 2026-08-31. Logged-out price is a <format:price/> placeholder. Used as a test fixture for the category-crawl discovery fallback.

nodes.label: Oakley SI Holbrook PDP fixture
nodes.rationale: Captured server-side-rendered PDP HTML for Standard Issue Holbrook (productCode W0OO9102OSI, retailer_item_id OO9102-B9), build 2026-08-27. Contains utag_data.Products / productObj with per-UPC variant data and a <format:price/> placeholder (login-gated price). Used as the PDP-parser test fixture.

nodes.label: _resolve_options / Option1-first packing
nodes.rationale: Crispi imported '0 products added' because size-only products had Option2 Name set with Option1 Name empty, which Shopify silently rejects. Fixed: options now pack into Option1 first, so a size-only boot is Option1 Name = Size.

nodes.label: Fixed price AUD $2,000 + ~$75 infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Rate AUD $22/hr (skilled PH-based dev, existing relationship); ~89 hrs total (~32 done + ~57 left). A Western scraping agency quotes AUD $7,000-10,000 for this job.

nodes.label: Reseller authorisation / indemnity confirmation
nodes.rationale: Real exposure is copyright - brands own their photos and copy; publishing is fine only if Broad Arrow is an authorised stockist of each. Client must get that in writing plus an indemnity clause. Client's responsibility.

nodes.label: Oakley image hosting options A/B/C
nodes.rationale: A: contractor hosts temporarily on own bucket, deleted after import confirmed, $0 (default). B: bucket kept live 3-6 months as re-import safety net, few AUD/month passed through. C: client infrastructure (storage bucket or Shopify upload token), images permanent on their side.

nodes.label: SKU column fill question (a/b/c)
nodes.rationale: For Crispi and Oakley clothing/footwear there is no per-size code on the source site. Client picks: (a) repeat the model/colour code on every size row [default], (b) generate a size code by pattern e.g. CR92H-42, (c) leave blank and their team assigns. Most Shopify setups do (c) or (a).

nodes.label: Phased delivery option (3 phases)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 Princeton Tec + Crispi ($350) lands first so the client sees the import working before committing to Phase 2 eyewear ($900) and Phase 3 apparel/accessories/footwear/goggles ($750). Lower risk for both sides.

nodes.label: Akamai circuit breaker (abort after 3 blocked requests)
nodes.norm_label: akamai circuit breaker (abort after 3 blocked requests)
nodes.rationale: After 3 consecutive Akamai-blocked requests it aborts in ~30s and keeps what was scraped, replacing 20+ min of exponential backoff; a 0-product run is not written so the last good file survives.

nodes.label: Oakley image re-hosting pipeline (Cloudflare R2)
nodes.rationale: Scrape-only engagement so images can't go in the client's Shopify Files. Pipeline: download origin PNG (plain Accept header) -> flatten to white JPEG, cap ~1600px q85 -> upload to Cloudflare R2 (boto3) -> rewrite CSV Image Src / Variant Image to public bucket URLs, torn down ~2-4 weeks after import. R2 free tier = $0.

nodes.label: ScraperAPI unblocker (SCRAPERAPI_KEY)
nodes.rationale: Chosen anti-bot path: make_fetcher() routes every request through ScraperAPI which solves Akamai and returns HTML; free tier 5,000 credits covers all 1,541 URLs at 1 credit/request.

nodes.label: Oakley /en-us/sitemap.xml product discovery
nodes.rationale: Sitemap yields all 1,541 product URLs in one request with lastmod for incremental runs, replacing a ~160-request category crawl; falls back to the category crawl if unavailable.

nodes.label: size-button PDP markup (softgoods size axis source)
nodes.norm_label: size-button pdp markup (softgoods size axis source)
nodes.rationale: Recon 2026-09-10: sizes live in <label class="size-button" data-size data-variant=<13-digit EAN> data-hasstock data-sku="">, one per size (repeated ~3x in DOM). Per-size barcode present, per-size SKU empty. Currently stubbed (option2=""); it is a parser gap, not a blocked-data gap.

nodes.label: Per-size EAN barcode present in data-variant, per-size SKU empty
nodes.norm_label: per-size ean barcode present in data-variant, per-size sku empty
nodes.rationale: Each size-button carries a distinct UPC/EAN in data-variant (e.g. 888896848209 for size 6, 888896848124 for size 6.5) while data-sku is always empty - so barcodes are covered per size but no size-level SKU exists to scrape.

nodes.label: size-button element markup (data-size / data-variant / data-sku)
nodes.rationale: <label class="size-button select-checkbox" data-checked="false" data-size="6" data-sku="" data-variant="888896848209" data-hasstock="true"> - one per size, 12-digit UPC in data-variant, data-sku always empty.

nodes.label: Risk 13 - image hosting (BLOCKER)
nodes.rationale: ~12k Oakley images must be served somewhere Shopify can fetch during import (not oakleysi.com - AVIF). Shopify copies each image to its own CDN on success, so hosting is only for the import window. Options: A (our R2, deleted after, $0, default), B (keep R2 3-6 months as re-import safety net), C (client bucket or Shopify upload token). Confirm before the full run.

nodes.label: Risk 1 - Oakley price login-gated (ID.me)
nodes.rationale: Oakley price is behind ID.me (active military / gov / first responder - cannot register), rendered as an empty <format:price/> placeholder logged-out. Everything else renders logged-out. Prices later = a client price list, or a logged-in session we drive (+6-10 hrs). So Oakley + Crispi land blank, Princeton Tec lands as USD RRP.

nodes.label: Risk 2 - Akamai no longer a project risk
nodes.norm_label: risk 2 - akamai no longer a project risk
nodes.rationale: ScraperAPI tested end to end: clean pages, real product data, 1 credit/request. One crawl ~1,542 credits; project with dev re-runs needs ~6-10k, so run one month of the Hobby plan ($49/100k credits), cancelled on delivery. Circuit breaker + partial-write mean a hiccup costs ~30s and never loses scraped work.

nodes.label: Risk 4 - Crispi = 13 products (whole AU site)
nodes.rationale: The brief's 'Cirspi / cirspiaustralia.com.au' does not resolve; real site is crispiaustralia.com.au. 13 products verified via store API + category counts is the entire AU catalogue. Crispi globally makes 40+ models - the full range is a different site (crispi.com), re-scoped. Confirm which catalogue.

nodes.label: Risk 5 - Oakley size variants are in the SSR HTML
nodes.norm_label: risk 5 - oakley size variants are in the ssr html
nodes.rationale: Parser handles eyewear (one-size) today. ~580 products (apparel 310, footwear 35, goggles) need the size axis parsed and exploded colour x size. Recon 2026-09-10 confirms data is in SSR HTML (size-button label with data-size/data-variant/data-hasstock, per-size barcode) - straight parser work, no extra requests, no blocked data. ~8-10 hrs.

nodes.label: Risk 6 - Oakley colourway grouping
nodes.rationale: Oakley lists each colour of a model as its own product page. Default = mirror the source (one Shopify product per colourway). Grouping into one product with a Colour option adds ~4 hrs. Confirm preference.

nodes.label: Risk 9 - per-variant SKUs differ by brand
nodes.norm_label: risk 9 - per-variant skus differ by brand
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-09-10. Princeton Tec: real per-size SKUs, finish as costed. Crispi: none exist to scrape, finest is model-level code, removes the 'parse the variation form' line. Oakley softgoods: same, data-sku="", only colour-level SKU. Client decision put to Howard: (a) model code on every row [default], (b) synthesise by convention, (c) leave blank.

nodes.label: Akamai Bot Manager wall
nodes.rationale: Oakley SI sits behind Akamai Bot Manager: plain requests get HTTP 403, curl_cffi lasts ~40-50 requests then gets a JS-challenge stub; only a real/stealthed browser sustains access. This is why proxies / an unblocker / cookie-seeding are needed for a full 1,400-product run.

nodes.label: Oakley CDN AVIF format Shopify rejects
nodes.norm_label: oakley cdn avif format shopify rejects
nodes.rationale: assets*.oakley.com does Accept-header negotiation and serves AVIF, which Shopify rejects ("Media processing failed"). Query params force origin PNG but don't survive Shopify's CSV importer. Hence images must be re-hosted.

nodes.label: Per-variant SKU known gap
nodes.rationale: Verified 2026-09-10: Princeton Tec has real per-size SKUs (Store API exposes most, rest from product page). Crispi has NO per-size SKUs at any layer - finest is model-level code (CR65V-1, CR92H). Oakley softgoods same - size buttons carry data-sku="", only colour-level SKU exists. Synthesised size rows therefore cannot get a real SKU; client decides (repeat model code / synthesise by convention / leave blank).

nodes.label: clean_description() page-builder stripping
nodes.rationale: Strips page-builder scaffolding (Magento PageBuilder, Avada/Fusion Builder), keeps headings/lists/paragraphs. Also no longer appends the separate .sizeText block when .singleContent already contains frame/lens measurements (fixed duplicate-measurements bug).

nodes.label: _product_type() Shopify Type mapping
nodes.rationale: Maps the product_category code's most specific known segment (_CATEGORY_SEGMENTS) to a Type; falls back to data-sizecategory, then a promo-filtered breadcrumb. validate.py promo-Type smells went 13/20 -> 0.

nodes.label: tools/validate.py QA script
nodes.rationale: Reports BLOCKERS (Shopify silently rejects: no Title, duplicate variant options, Option2-without-Option1) and SMELLS (no images, bad prices, promo-collection Type values). Exits non-zero on any blocker. Optional --images HEAD-check and --sitemap coverage diff.

nodes.label: QA across 1,541 products (biggest single item)
nodes.rationale: ~12 hrs: validation script + sampling + fixing bad rows. At catalogue volume you can't just eyeball it. Final QA pass also re-checks the sitemap and picks up any add/remove delta before delivery.

nodes.label: Colour swatch title attribute as colour name
nodes.norm_label: colour swatch title attribute as colour name
nodes.rationale: Colour swatch links on the main page carry the real name in title="Blackout", no extra fetch. utag_data.Products FrameColor is empty for softgoods (only populated for eyewear), which is why current fallback labels are junk. Not started.

nodes.label: utag_data.product_category taxonomy code
nodes.rationale: A stable code (oo_afa_foot_boot, oo_afa_app_topw_tshirt_lifestyle) that survives promo breadcrumbs, unlike the .breadcrumb path which routes many products through promo collections.

nodes.label: utag_data.Products embedded JS object
nodes.rationale: Each PDP embeds utag_data.Products keyed by UPC with Sku/FrameColor/LensColor/Category/ModelName; parsed with a brace-matcher because it is a JS object literal with unquoted numeric keys, not JSON. Gives per-variant barcodes + attributes with no login.

nodes.label: Empty FrameColor for softgoods in utag_data.Products
nodes.norm_label: empty framecolor for softgoods in utag_data.products
nodes.rationale: FrameColor is "" in this footwear PDP's utag_data.Products, confirming the README note that FrameColor is only populated for eyewear - the reason softgoods colour names must come from the swatch title attribute.

nodes.label: Promo breadcrumb path (Holiday Gifts for Tactical Missions)
nodes.norm_label: promo breadcrumb path (holiday gifts for tactical missions)
nodes.rationale: utag_data breadcrumb_path = 'Home / Landing / Holiday Gifts for Tactical Missions / Top Performing Gear / SI Light Patrol Boot' - a promo route that would give a junk Type, demonstrating why the taxonomy code is preferred.

nodes.label: product_category code oo_afa_foot_boot
nodes.rationale: utag_data "product_category":["oo_afa_foot_boot"] (and product_brand "osi_afa_foot_boot") - the stable taxonomy code that _product_type() maps to a Shopify Type.

nodes.label: utag_data.Products object (colour-level Sku 11190-02E, empty Price)
nodes.rationale: Products keyed by UPC (888896848100) with Category AFA, Sku 11190-02E, ModelName 'SI Light Patrol Boot', empty Price/PriceFull (login-gated), and empty FrameColor/LensColor/LensTechnology for this footwear product.

nodes.label: SI Light Patrol Boot PDP fixture (style 11190, Blackout)
nodes.norm_label: si light patrol boot pdp fixture (style 11190, blackout)
nodes.rationale: Saved SSR PDP for Oakley SI footwear used as a parser test fixture. Style code 11190, colour-level SKU 11190-02E, 16 sizes 6-13.5, canonical https://www.oakley.com/en-us/product/11190.

nodes.label: Promo breadcrumb unreliability
nodes.rationale: The .breadcrumb path is unreliable for Type because many products route through promo collections (Home / Landing / Holiday Gifts for Tactical Missions / ...). Drove the switch to the taxonomy code as the primary Type source.
